fatal_errors: The proposed AlCoCrFeNiMo alloy contains no titanium, so it cannot form in situ TiB2 without an unreported titanium addition.
The hypothesis replaces the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 L12/B2 eutectic alloy and DS2205 comparator with an unrelated boron-modified coating system.
Boron addition and thermal processing are changed together, preventing attribution of any effect to either intervention.
The cited dynamic-amorphization evidence concerns CoCrFeMnNi sliding in ultra-high vacuum and does not support continuous passive-film regeneration in saline tribocorrosion.
The experiment does not quantitatively separate total tribocorrosion loss into mechanical wear, corrosion, and interaction components.
explanation: The response addresses the broad idea that near-surface structure and passivation can govern combined wear-corrosion resistance, and it proposes a nominally matched control with tribological and electrochemical measurements. However, it does not reconstruct the relevant material, thermal-shock treatment, DS2205 baseline, deionized-water conditions, temperature/load/frequency matrix, or the nonmonotonic minimum in degradation near 50 °C. Its central TiB2 mediator is chemically impossible for the stated Ti-free composition. Evidence E1 only broadly supports boron-related coating improvement and does not establish the specific TiB2/amorphization mechanism; E2 supports deformation-induced nanostructuring under inert ultra-high-vacuum wear, not corrosion passivation. The test also confounds composition with processing, and its falsification rule is overly stringent because failure of one claimed mechanism or performance component should be sufficient to challenge the hypothesis.
